subject: ADR-199: what the page said back -- an act is answerable for the message it raised, and twenty message boxes nobody was announcing
body: Every page in this kit answers a refusal in a transient message -- 'A stem needs a DBH', 'No stems to export', 'Both partners are needed' -- and the door could not hear one. `activate` answered ok:true, which says the CONTROL TOOK THE PRESS and says nothing about whether the page did what the press asked; the two were the same answer. The message lives 1.7 seconds, so it could not be fetched afterwards either -- which is why three tasks in this kit are written as a whole read-report taken inside that window against a box holding whatever the LAST message was, a race dressed as a claim. THE CHANNEL IS THE LIVE REGION, NOT THE CLASS NAME: querySelector ('.toast') would have passed every check in this slice and been wrong on the first page written with a role=log line or an alert bar, so the door reads the platform's own definition -- role=status, role=alert, aria-live other than off. That decision produced the finding, because reading the standard means asking which pages meet it: TWENTY OF THE KIT'S TWENTY-ONE transient message elements were plain divs, announced to no screen reader and invisible to the door, and only experiment-guide.html had ever declared one. All twenty now carry role=status aria-live=polite, and nineteen also SHIPPED WITH TEXT IN THEM ('Saved', 'Copied') -- a live region is in the accessibility tree whether or not it is on screen, so placeholder text there is a sentence a reader can find before anything has been saved. Two fields on every act: `said`, spliced at the end because a message belongs to the act it was raised during exactly as a payload does; and `produced`, a MONOTONIC COUNTER READ EITHER SIDE OF THE ACT rather than the length of the outbox, because collect-output splices the outbox and its length reports somebody else's backlog -- two exports with the first still uncollected are one and one, not one and two. THE SAME REFUSAL TWICE IS TWO REFUSALS: the first draft skipped a message identical to the one still on screen and the stand sheet's second 'A stem needs a DBH' vanished, which is ADR-100's fault exactly -- the reasoning that once accused twelve live controls of being wired to nothing. One entry per observer callback instead, verified empirically. Checked in three registers: the kit's source, scanned through the docs directory THE RUN IS SERVING so a page mutant behind CSRBT_DOCS_DIR cannot hide; the stand sheet and the collection sheet through the gateway; and a BUILT FIXTURE carrying role=log, a bare role=alert and an undeclared div, where the first two are heard and the third must not be, since a door reporting it would be inventing an accessibility the page does not have. verify_report 223 -> 237, mutate_report 134 -> 141, all seven new mutants killed. Twenty artifacts republished and measured at the URL.
